The PID circuit uses a series of operational amplifiers to reshape the error signal. The output signal should have a fast rise time, low overshoot, and the correct gain that reaches the desired set point value...
The use of a quad operational amplifier (OP AMP) provides for the proportional, integral, and derivative actions. The quad OP AMP amplifies and combines the PID signals
The PID control system uses an LM3403 Quad OP AMP. The LM3403 integrated circuit consists of four independent high-gain, operational amplifiers.
The PID summing amplifier is a standard LM741 OP AMP. The LM741 consists of a single operational amplifier that provides amplification and isolation of the combined PID signal.
's look at the block diagram for the PID Control System.

This experiment demonstrates the use of the PID control system as a servo motor controller. Throughout the remainder of the lesson the schematic diagrams may be brought up at any time by pressing Ctrl S (Holding the computer keyboard Ctrl key while pressing the S key). Let's look at the block diagram for the PID Control System..
The Position controller sends a set point (reference position) to the Window decoder. The Position detector sends the process variable signal to the Window decoder.
The Window decoder processes the two signals and only sends an error signal to the PID controller if a difference voltage is present.

The error signal sent to the proportional control is processed into a gain input to the summing amplifier.

The error signal sent to the integral control is processed into a reset signal. The derivative control processes the reset signal from the integral control and outputs a rate signal to the summing amplifier.....

The Summing amplifier combines and amplifies the input signals into an actuator signal and sends it to the Pulse Width Modulator (PWM). The PWM, sends the pulse width modulated actuator signal to the H-Switch/Amplifier...

The H-Switch/Amplifier processes the PWM signal into a directional encoding and amplification signal to the motor. The closed loop cycle is repeated as the Position Detector senses and processes a new variable signal to the Window decoder...
